Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Peaches and possible persimmon

Elders remembered peach trees, cooking with peaches, selling baskets in town, and trading fruit with other growers. On the same page, “possible persimmon” appears as a separate heading with three recorded word forms.1

The page attributes the persimmon forms to Powhatan and broader Algonquian sources rather than to Shinnecock speakers.1

Places named in the catalogue

Location unknown.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF p. 16. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
